title: Maximal generalizations inside an arbitrary subset of a Noetherian scheme
statement: Let $U$ be a Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme], meaning a quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme] locally Noetherian scheme [pqf-def-locnoeth]. For every subset $T\subseteq |U|$ and every $t\in T$, there exists $m\in T$ such that $t\in\overline{\{m\}}$ and, for every $s\in T$, the implication $m\in\overline{\{s\}}\Longrightarrow s=m$ holds. The bar denotes closure in $|U|$; thus the assertion chooses a generalization of $t$ which has no proper generalization in $T$. No closedness or constructibility of $T$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0G2R, lemma-maximal-points, assertion (b), with the definition of T_0 in its statement; the undefined T' there is read as T, as required by the proof.

proof.text: For each $x\in U$, choose from the locally Noetherian affine cover an affine neighbourhood $V$ with Noetherian ring $A=\mathcal O_U(V)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization], the germ map $A\to\mathcal O_{U,x}$ is a localization at the prime of $x$. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian] makes $\mathcal O_{U,x}$ Noetherian. It is a local ring since $U$ is a scheme. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-local-finite-krull-dimension] to obtain a natural number $d(x)=\dim\mathcal O_{U,x}$ for each $x$. No bound independent of $x$ is asserted.

By [lem-sc-scheme-stalk-dimension-generalization-chains], $d(x)$ is the supremum of lengths of strict generalization chains starting at $x$. These lengths contain $0$ and are natural numbers bounded by the finite integer $d(x)$; hence their supremum is attained. If $y\ne x$ and $x\in\overline{\{y\}}$, prepend $x$ to a chain of length $d(y)$ starting at $y$. This is a strict generalization chain of length $d(y)+1$ starting at $x$, so $d(y)+1\le d(x)$. Consequently every proper generalization strictly decreases $d$.

Fix $t\in T$ and set $G=\{x\in T:t\in\overline{\{x\}}\}$. Reflexivity of singleton closure gives $t\in G$. The nonempty subset $\{d(x):x\in G\}\subseteq\mathbf N$ has a least element; choose $m\in G$ realizing it. Thus $m\in T$ and $t\in\overline{\{m\}}$, and $d(m)\le d(x)$ for all $x\in G$.

Let $s\in T$ satisfy $m\in\overline{\{s\}}$. Singleton-closure specialization is transitive: since $\overline{\{m\}}\subseteq\overline{\{s\}}$, we have $t\in\overline{\{s\}}$ and hence $s\in G$. If $s\ne m$, step 2 gives $d(s)<d(m)$, contradicting the minimality in step 3. Therefore $s=m$, giving the required maximality in $T$.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q90-86bfdc3e3 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read Stacks properties.tex Tag 0G2R (lemma-maximal-points) in full; the delivery reads its typos T' as T and O_{T,t'} as O_{S,t'}, which is correct. The statement is unchanged and is assertion (b) of the source, with nothing weakened or strengthened. Step 1: pqf-def-locnoeth gives an affine V with Noetherian ring A. Clause (c) of affine-open-stalk-localization (Mathlib isLocalization_stalk) gives exactly the hypotheses (a)-(c) of localization-noetherian at A minus p_x, so the stalk is Noetherian. It is local because a scheme is a locally ringed space, so noetherian-local-finite-krull-dimension (KrullsHeightTheorem:276) gives d(x) in N. All cited nodes are Mathlib leaves or definitions, so there is no route issue and no tool_uses is needed. Step 2: the cited node lem-sc-scheme-stalk-dimension-generalization-chains (ringKrullDim_stalk_eq_coheight) defines dim O_{X,x} as the supremum of chain lengths. The supremum is attained, and I checked that putting x in front of a chain starting at y gives d(y)+1 <= d(x), so the orientation is right. Steps 3 and 4: G = {x in T : t in cl{x}} contains t, a minimizer of d over G is m, and transitivity of specialization puts any generalization s of m in G, so s = m. This makes explicit the restriction to T that the source leaves implicit. Edge cases checked: empty T, singleton T, a field, a DVR with T = {eta, s} or {s}, infinite sets of closed points. Quasi-compactness is unused, which is harmless.
